chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who is in his salat and a pumpkin seed comes out from him: there is nothing upon him, and it has not invalidated his wudu (ablution). But if it comes out smeared with excrement, then he must repeat the wudu (ablution), and if he is in his salat, he must cut off the salat, and repeat the wudu (ablution) and the salat.
Then he said, may Allah, Exalted is He, support him: if he does that intentionally, then he must purify himself and recommence the salat from its beginning.

When it is established, by what will indicate it later, that these matters—namely speech done deliberately, or turning so as to face away from the qiblah intentionally, or causing an occurrence among those things that cut off the salat—then it is established that recommencing it is obligatory. We shall mention later, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills, what indicates that in a manner that is sufficient, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.

key_terms.الْعَذِرَةِ: excrement, ritual impurity whose presence affects the legal ruling
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the qiblah, the direction faced in salat
key_terms.حَبُّ الْقَرْعِ: a pumpkin seed, used here as an example of a dry object exiting the body
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being discussed
key_terms.قَطَعَ الصَّلَاةَ: he cut off the salat, meaning he must discontinue the prayer
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: his wudu (ablution), the state of ritual purity before salat
key_terms.يَتَطَهَّرَ: to purify himself, meaning to restore ritual purity
key_terms.يَسْتَأْنِفَ الصَّلَاةَ: to recommence the salat from the beginning

ai.seo_question: What happens to wudu (ablution) and salat if something exits the body during prayer?
ai.summary: This passage gives a legal ruling about what exits from a person during salat and whether it invalidates wudu (ablution) and the prayer. It distinguishes between a dry object exiting without impurity, which does not nullify wudu (ablution), and that which exits smeared with excrement, which requires repeating both wudu (ablution) and salat; it also affirms that deliberate acts that invalidate salat require restarting it from the beginning.
